description: Ten varied tickets representing an undirected sample of a small-business MSP queue, with security incidents mixed among routine support requests. Written by GPT-5 Codex for Summit Managed IT evaluation.

provenance.author: GPT-5 Codex, 2026-08-10
materials_withheld: the system under evaluation, its implementation and prompts, prior evaluation corpora, and evaluation results
provenance.isolation: Work was confined by instruction and filesystem scope to a dedicated directory containing only the task brief, KB-006, the format specification, the template, and the output folder.
provenance.known_leakage: No scenario direction was supplied. The commissioner excluded all bank, payment, and remittance-change cases and required at least two of four incident cases to fall outside KB-006's examples; the exclusion removed one common queue topic and therefore constrained the sample somewhat, while the outside-list quota influenced incident selection more materially. No outside material or prior project knowledge was used.

cases.subject: shared folder wont take my password
cases.body: Megan sent me a SharePoint document and it asked me to sign in again. I put my email password in twice but it just went back to the same page. Can you make the folder open?
cases.rationale: The user entered credentials into a suspicious sign-in page reached from an unsolicited link, requiring immediate escalation.

cases.subject: cad archive broken overnight
cases.body: All the job drawings on the shared drive have .qq7 after their names this morning and none will open. There is also a HOW_TO_GET_THEM_BACK text file in every folder. Night shift says they didn't touch it.
cases.rationale: Widespread unusable files with a new suffix and recovery instructions indicate an active destructive compromise.

cases.subject: laptop missing from van
cases.body: Call from field supervisor: his work laptop was taken from the van at lunch. He says the lid was open and his scheduling screen was already logged in. He is at the police station and wants a loaner for tomorrow.
cases.rationale: The theft of an unlocked, authenticated company laptop creates an immediate exposure not specifically enumerated in KB-006.

cases.subject: mouse moving when i wasnt
cases.body: I came back from the copier and the pointer was moving through employee payroll folders by itself. It opened two staff records while my hands were off the mouse, then stopped when I shut the laptop. Nobody from support had called me.
cases.rationale: Unrequested remote control browsing sensitive records is a suspected active compromise outside KB-006's named examples.

cases.subject: voicemail attachment issue
cases.body: I opened the voicemail spreadsheet from Curtis and clicked Enable so I could hear it. A black window flashed a few times and now Excel closes whenever I type. Curtis replied that his new phone system does this and the file is safe, so it probably only needs Office repaired.
cases.rationale: A purported attachment was opened and immediately followed by changed computer behavior; the alleged sender's reassurance does not remove the incident.

cases.subject: screen keeps going black
cases.body: My right monitor goes black if I raise the standing desk, then comes back when I push the cable in. Left one is fine. Could someone bring a longer lead?
cases.rationale: This is a reproducible loose-cable hardware issue, not malicious screen behavior or another security incident.

cases.subject: vpn unavailable tonight
cases.body: VPN says service unavailable from home. The IT banner says maintenance 8-10 tonight and it is 8:20, but I need to know whether I should wait or drive in.
cases.rationale: The connection failure occurs inside a posted maintenance window and does not describe any suspected security activity.

cases.subject: locked myself out sorry
cases.body: I got the account locked message after trying my password over and over. Just noticed Caps Lock was on the whole time, so yes this was me. The reset email arrived right after my last try; can you unlock it?
cases.rationale: This resembles an unauthorized lockout or reset alert, but the user explicitly accounts for both events through their own repeated attempts.
cases.kb006_bullet: unexplained account lock or reset notice

cases.subject: virus box in training
cases.body: The annual safety course shows a big red 'YOUR PC IS INFECTED' box when I reach the phishing lesson. It stays inside the course page and goes away when I close that tab. Is that the example I am supposed to click on or did I fail something?
cases.rationale: The warning is clearly content inside a known training lesson rather than a browser takeover, though its appearance resembles a fake alert.

cases.subject: i renamed the whole scan folder
cases.body: I ran our month-end archive tool and picked the date-only preset by mistake, so every PDF is now named like 2026-08-001 instead of the client name. They all still open and there isn't any message asking for anything. Can yesterday's names be put back?
cases.rationale: This resembles mass malicious renaming, but the user identifies the exact normal batch action, and the files remain usable with no coercive note.
